dossier.purpose: MCP server plus per-client hook/plugin set that keeps large tool output out of an AI coding agent's context. Code runs in a local subprocess and only stdout returns. Big outputs, docs and fetched URLs are chunked into a local SQLite FTS5 (BM25) store and queried back with ctx_search. Hooks record session events (files, tasks, git, errors, decisions) in per-project SQLite and rebuild a resume snapshot after compaction. Supports 17 clients (Claude Code and Codex CLI among them) plus an OpenClaw gateway plugin. Savings are reported as byte-derived estimates. Provider-reported token usage from Claude Code/Codex logs is captured by Stop hooks but no tool in this repo reports it (see code.architecture).

claims.claim: Context Mode is an MCP server that solves four problems: context saving, session continuity, think-in-code, and no prose-style enforcement; 'mandatory paradigm across all 17 supported clients, plus the OpenClaw gateway integration'.
"Sandbox tools keep raw data out of the context window. 315 KB becomes 5.4 KB. 98% reduction."

File edits, git ops, tasks, errors and decisions are tracked in SQLite; on compaction events are indexed into FTS5 and retrieved via BM25. "If you don't `--continue`, previous session data is deleted immediately — a fresh session means a clean slate."

The Claude Code plugin registers all hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, SessionStart, Stop) and 11 MCP tools: six sandbox tools plus ctx_stats, ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade, ctx_purge, ctx_insight.
/context-mode:ctx-stats gives "Context savings — per-tool breakdown, tokens consumed, savings ratio."
Optional status line: "The bar shows `$ saved this session · $ saved across sessions · % efficient`".

When output exceeds 5 KB and an `intent` is provided, the full output is indexed into the knowledge base, matching sections are searched, and only relevant matches plus a vocabulary of searchable terms are returned.

ctx_search returns snippets of 'the actual indexed content'; ranking merges Porter-stemmed and trigram FTS5 results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then proximity reranking and Levenshtein typo correction; titles/headings weighted 5x.

Indexed content persists in a per-project SQLite DB at ~/.context-mode/content/; fetch cache TTL defaults to 24 h; "14-day cleanup: Content databases and sources older than 14 days are removed on startup."
PreCompact builds a "priority-tiered XML snapshot (≤2 KB)"; if the 2 KB budget is tight, lower-priority events are dropped first.

Benchmark table: Playwright snapshot 56.2 KB -> 299 B (99%); GitHub issues 58.9 KB -> 1.1 KB (98%); access log 45.1 KB -> 155 B; repo research (subagent) 986 KB -> 62 KB (94%). "Over a full session: 315 KB of raw output becomes 5.4 KB. Session time extends from ~30 minutes to ~3 hours."
With hooks the routing saves ~98%; without hooks (instruction file only) ~60%.
"Nothing leaves your machine. No telemetry, no cloud sync, no usage tracking, no account required."

ctx_execute_file is confined to the project root (#852); ctx_execute/ctx_batch_execute run arbitrary code with the process's filesystem access, so the guard is 'not a full OS sandbox'; ctx_fetch_and_index blocks link-local/IMDS targets and, with CTX_FETCH_STRICT=1, loopback/RFC1918.

code.architecture: TypeScript in src/ is compiled by tsc to build/ and bundled (minified) by esbuild into server.bundle.mjs, cli.bundle.mjs and hooks/*.bundle.mjs. Key modules: src/server.ts (MCP server, 11 ctx_* tools, per-response byte accounting in trackResponse at :885-949, SSRF guard, project-boundary guard); src/executor.ts + src/runtime.ts (subprocess runner for 12 languages, env injection denylist, 100 MB output cap); src/store.ts (ContentStore: SQLite FTS5, chunks <= 4096 bytes, porter + trigram tables, bm25 title weight 5, RRF k=60, proximity rerank, Levenshtein correction); src/db-base.ts (bun:sqlite / node:sqlite / better-sqlite3 selection); src/session/{db,extract,snapshot,analytics,pricing}.ts (per-project session DB with session_events / session_meta / session_resume / tool_calls, event extractors, reference-based resume snapshot, ctx_stats report, vendored 61-row price table); src/adapters/* (17 client adapters plus per-adapter usage parsers); hooks/*.mjs (per-platform hooks); hooks/platform-bridge.mjs; bin/statusline.mjs. RECOVERABLE ORIGINALS: ctx_index, ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file with `intent` and output > 5 KB, any output > 100 KB, and ctx_fetch_and_index persist the full text as verbatim chunks in the local FTS5 store, retrievable with ctx_search (src/server.ts:1883-1935, 1979-1980; thresholds INTENT 5,000 B and LARGE 102,400 B). Content DBs older than 14 days are deleted at server start (src/server.ts:726-730); ctx_purge wipes on request. ctx_execute output <= 100 KB without intent is returned inline and not stored (src/server.ts:1937-1941). Native-tool (Bash/Read) outputs are not stored in full, only short extracted event strings (README.md:1258-1285), capped at 1000 events per session with lowest-priority eviction (src/session/db.ts:639). ctx_search is progressively throttled: results reduced after 3 calls and refused after 8 within a 60 s window, env-tunable (src/server.ts:2457-2459). Resume snapshot is a reference-based table of contents with runnable ctx_search calls, not size-capped (src/session/snapshot.ts:12-14, 470). PROVIDER-USAGE ANSWER: no single user-facing tool (MCP tool, slash command, CLI subcommand or statusline) reports provider-reported token usage, so the answer to 'which single tool' is none. Passive capture exists: hooks/stop.mjs (Claude Code Stop) reads the hook's transcript_path JSONL and sums message.usage input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens per model over non-sidechain assistant lines (src/session/extract.ts:2096-2194; hooks/stop.mjs:51-72). hooks/codex/stop.mjs reads $CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/rollout-*-<session>.jsonl token_count events (src/adapters/codex/usage.ts: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens -> cache_read, output + reasoning_output -> output, cache_creation always 0) and loads only build/adapters/codex/usage.js (hooks/codex/stop.mjs:63-76), which is absent from a plain git checkout (build/ is git-ignored, .gitignore:2) and from the committed session-extract bundle. Both emit 'agent_usage' events (category 'cost'); locally these persist only as a text string 'tokens_in:.. tokens_out:.. cache_create:.. cache_read:.. cost_usd:..' in session_events.data (no token columns, no model id in the string; src/session/extract.ts:1921-1943; src/session/db.ts:827-843, 915-922); typed fields are forwarded only when ~/.context-mode/platform.json exists. Nothing in src/ or bin/ reads them back, so ctx_stats and the statusline show byte-derived estimates (tokens = bytes/4; 256 tokens per captured event; src/session/analytics.ts:459, 2696). Artifact reduction (bytes_avoided / bytes_returned) and provider usage are therefore never joined or reported together.

risks: Provider-usage gap: the only provider-token capture is passive (Claude/Codex Stop hooks) and nothing in src/ or bin/ reads the agent_usage events back. Locally they survive only as text in session_events.data (no token columns, no model id), capped at 1000 events/session with lowest-priority eviction and deleted with sessions older than 7 days (src/session/db.ts:639, 827-843, 1696); typed fields leave only via the opt-in forwarder. Codex capture needs build/adapters/codex/usage.js, which a plain git/marketplace checkout lacks (hooks/codex/stop.mjs:63-76; .gitignore:2; start.mjs:466-470). MCP-only Claude installs have no hooks and therefore no capture (README.md:120).

Usage-capture accuracy is unverified: the transcript parser sums every non-sidechain assistant line with no message.id/requestId de-duplication (src/session/extract.ts:2045-2059, 2128-2144) and its only fixture is synthetic with one line per message id (tests/fixtures/claude-code-transcript.jsonl). After transcript compaction a lost cursor falls back to only the last turn (extract.ts:2166-2168). Sub-agent usage is captured separately as 'task_cumulative' without cost (extract.ts:1539-1570). Codex has no cache-creation bucket (src/adapters/codex/usage.ts:106-108). cost_usd comes from a vendored 61-row price table and unknown model ids get no cost (src/session/pricing.ts:12-25).

Savings figures are partly modelled, not measured: hook redirects credit hard-coded bytes (8192 for curl/wget, 16384 for WebFetch) and the full file size for Read calls that are only nudged, not blocked (hooks/core/routing.mjs:779, 853-861, 886; hooks/pretooluse.mjs:203-204 calls it 'estimated'); indexed bytes count as 'kept out' (src/server.ts:951-961); tokens = bytes/4 and 256 per event (src/session/analytics.ts:459, 2696). ADR-0004 shows the headline formula changed between versions (56% -> 95.4% on the same data). All benchmark numbers are project-reported; no independent measurement found in the repo.

Network/egress is broader than README.md:1524 implies: hourly npm-registry version check with no opt-out found (src/server.ts:4956-4959); an undocumented opt-in forwarder POSTs every event, including token/cost fields and git-remote-derived project identity, to a configured platform_url (hooks/platform-bridge.mjs:268-308); a hosted 'Insight' product with sign-in/pricing is opened by ctx_insight (src/server.ts:4814; skills/ctx-insight/SKILL.md:23); code comments tie usage capture to a paid-observability/FinOps platform (src/adapters/codex/usage.ts:11-12; hooks/session-loaders.mjs:146-149).

Supply chain and release hygiene: manual local npm publish with no provenance, signatures or checksums (.claude/skills/context-mode-ops/release.md:128-138); committed minified bundles built by a CI bot are what plugin installs run (.github/workflows/bundle.yml:34-41; start.mjs:600-602); `context-mode upgrade`/ctx_upgrade git-clones the default-branch HEAD and runs npm install + npm run build with no tag pin or signature check (src/cli.ts:1305-1373); runtime unpinned `npm install` of better-sqlite3 and turndown packages (hooks/ensure-deps.mjs:70-81; start.mjs:486-538); only bun.lock is committed while packageManager says pnpm and CI uses npm install (package.json:122; .gitignore:11; ci.yml:46-47).

Code-execution surface: ctx_execute/ctx_batch_execute run arbitrary code in 12 languages as the user, with the parent environment minus an injection denylist and the real HOME, explicitly 'not a full OS sandbox' (src/executor.ts:573-697; README.md:1575). The project-boundary guard covers only ctx_execute_file and fails open on resolver errors (src/server.ts:1180-1182, 1205-1207). .codex-plugin/mcp.json:10 sets default_tools_approval_mode 'approve' for the Codex plugin (effect depends on Codex semantics; not verified here). Hooks fail open by design (src/cli.ts:171-182) with opt-in fail-closed only via CONTEXT_MODE_REQUIRE_SECURITY=1 (hooks/core/routing.mjs:673-688).

Licensing: Elastic License 2.0 is source-available, not OSI-approved. It forbids offering the software as a hosted/managed service and removing licensor notices, and carries a license-key-circumvention clause (LICENSE:16-28). The licensor also runs a hosted commercial product (Insight, context-mode.com/insight).

Maintenance and doc drift: 17-client matrix, patch-release cadence (v1.0.169) and a single named author in manifests (package.json:6). Several docs disagree with code: statusline '$' vs bytes, '2 KB snapshot', 'deleted immediately', README's Linux-only node:sqlite vs any Node >= 22.5 (src/db-base.ts:273-279), docs/platform-support.md:42 lists Claude Code Stop as unsupported while hooks/hooks.json:131-141 registers it, BENCHMARK.md:120-139 cites 125 tests and npm scripts that do not exist versus 210 test files, plugin manifests say 11 languages versus 12 in src/runtime.ts:40-52. CI accepts non-zero vitest exits when the summary shows passed and retries tests twice on CI (ci.yml:61-96; vitest.config.ts:27).
